From 93bdc0eb0b4bb5e7094fd4a95f4a394e4a927e09 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Gustavo A. R. Silva" <gustavo@embeddedor.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Dec 2019 09:05:32 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] can: tcan4x5x: tcan4x5x_parse_config(): fix inconsistent
 IS_ERR and PTR_ERR

Fix inconsistent IS_ERR and PTR_ERR in tcan4x5x_parse_config().

The proper pointer to be passed as argument is tcan4x5x->device_wake_gpio.

This bug was detected with the help of Coccinelle.

Fixes: 2de497356955 ("can: tcan45x: Make wake-up GPIO an optional GPIO")
Signed-off-by: Gustavo A. R. Silva <gustavo@embeddedor.com>
Acked-by: Dan Murphy <dmurphy@ti.com>
Signed-off-by: Marc Kleine-Budde <mkl@pengutronix.de>

diff --git a/drivers/net/can/m_can/tcan4x5x.c b/drivers/net/can/m_can/tcan4x5x.c
index a413e7548546..eacd428e07e9 100644
--- a/drivers/net/can/m_can/tcan4x5x.c
+++ b/drivers/net/can/m_can/tcan4x5x.c
@@ -387,7 +387,7 @@ static int tcan4x5x_parse_config(struct m_can_classdev *cdev)
 	tcan4x5x->device_wake_gpio = devm_gpiod_get(cdev->dev, "device-wake",
 						    GPIOD_OUT_HIGH);
 	if (IS_ERR(tcan4x5x->device_wake_gpio)) {
-		if (PTR_ERR(tcan4x5x->power) == -EPROBE_DEFER)
+		if (PTR_ERR(tcan4x5x->device_wake_gpio) == -EPROBE_DEFER)
 			return -EPROBE_DEFER;
 
 		tcan4x5x_disable_wake(cdev);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/net/can/m_can/tcan4x5x.c`**
- The line checking for the error condition of `device_wake_gpio` was modified. 
- The original code used `PTR_ERR(tcan4x5x->power)` to check for the error condition, which was incorrect.
- The modified code now correctly uses `PTR_ERR(tcan4x5x->device_wake_gpio)` to check if the error is due to `device_wake_gpio` being set to an error value.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The modification addresses a bug related to error handling in the `tcan4x5x_parse_config()` function. 
- By correcting the pointer used in the error check, the patch ensures that the function properly identifies when the `device_wake_gpio` initialization fails, leading to more accurate error reporting and handling in the driver. 
- This change is part of a broader fix indicated by the commit message, which references a previous commit that made the wake-up GPIO optional, highlighting the importance of maintaining consistent error handling in the context of recent changes.

```c

    if (PTR_ERR(tcan4x5x->power) == -EPROBE_DEFER)
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the code incorrectly checks the error condition using `tcan4x5x->power` instead of `tcan4x5x->device_wake_gpio`. This inconsistency means that if the initialization of `device_wake_gpio` fails, the error handling may not trigger correctly, leading to potential misbehavior of the driver.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (IS_ERR(tcan4x5x->device_wake_gpio)) {
    if (PTR_ERR(tcan4x5x->device_wake_gpio) == -EPROBE_DEFER)
```
Reason:
The fix involves changing the pointer used in the error handling check from `tcan4x5x->power` to `tcan4x5x->device_wake_gpio`. This ensures that the error condition is checked correctly, allowing the driver to handle the failure of `device_wake_gpio` initialization properly, thus preventing misbehavior.
